note: Wikimedia Commons, “Eleuterus of Illyria (Menologion of Basil).jpg”; artist as recorded there: Authors of Menologion of Basil II (circa 985 AC, Constantinople), Byzantine manuscript illuminators[1]:  Pantoleon with Georgios, Michael the Younger, Michael of Blachernae, Symeon, Symeon of Blachernae, Menas, and Nestor    (Online on Vatican site) — fetched 03 October 2026 at 1200px. The licence is as Commons records it. Identified as this saint because: Commons' own description reads «Сщмч. Елевферий, еп. Иллирийский» - hieromartyr Eleutherius, bishop of Illyricum - and the file sits in Category:Eleuterus of Illyria. The see is exactly this folder's office line, which rules out the other Eleutherii: the pope, Eleutherius of Tournai, and the companion of Dionysius of Paris. It is a miniature from the Menologion of Basil II (Vat. gr. 1613, p. 246, c. 985). The 1903-1911 Russian plate set has no Eleutherius for the folder's feast of 15 December - its 04151 is a Stephen - so the Menologion stands in for it. Commons describes it: Сщмч. Елевферий, еп. Иллирийский. Миниатюра из Минология Василия II. 976-1025 гг. (Vat. gr. 1613. P.246) // Eleuterus of Illyria
